subject: LLM onramp options: VPC peering / PrivateLink / site-to-site VPN — recommendation and next steps
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@dataforge.io>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: dataforge-infra@dataforge.io
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onramp approach for private deployment (quick ask)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We are kicking off an evaluation for a private Redwood deployment and need a concise recommendation for network onramp: our options are VPC Peering, PrivateLink/Interface Endpoint, or a classical site-to-site VPN/IPSec.

High level constraints:
- Regulated PII workloads, need short path latency for inference (50-80ms RT target from app tier)
- Strict egress controls; Palo Alto firewalled datacenter
- Support for bursty batch workloads and occasional large model weights pulls (S3-like access)
- We prefer the lowest operational footprint on our side but can own limited config changes in network/firewall.

Can you send a short pros/cons + recommended path and what Redwood would need to do to POC? We have NetOps on copy.

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Infrastructure, DataForge
oliver.grant@dataforge.io

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@dataforge.io>
Cc: dataforge-infra@dataforge.io
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp approach for private deployment (quick ask)

Oliver — thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a concise comparison and our recommended path for an initial POC.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Primary: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) into a dedicated Redwood VPC with endpoint services.
- Fallback/secondary: Encrypted site-to-site (IPSec) VPN as a resilience path and for administrative traffic.

Why this combo?
- PrivateLink gives you strong surface reduction (no cross-VPC routing, enforced by endpoint), predictable TLS-terminated tunnels, and minimal NAT/flow changes on your side.
- S2S VPN provides a low-effort fallback that your NetOps team can stand up quickly and helps with large artifact pulls if routing/policy for PrivateLink blocks egress to cloud storage.

Quick pros/cons (one-liners):
- VPC Peering: lowest latency in same cloud accounts, but expands attack surface (routing across VPC) and complicates IP ownership; not ideal if you need strict tenant isolation or cloud-account separation.
- PrivateLink: best isolation and least exposed surface; a bit more upfront work to publish endpoint services and ensure security groups, but operationally cleaner.
- Site-to-site VPN: fast to bootstrap, easy for NetOps, less granular control and higher latency/MTU considerations; good for temporary or admin-only fallback.

POC kickoff checklist (what Redwood will do):
1) Create a dedicated Redwood VPC and expose the model service as an endpoint service (PrivateLink).
2) Share endpoint service name and a short deployment guide for Security Groups and allowed CIDR ranges.
3) Stand up a temporary pre-production VPN endpoint (managed by Redwood) we can use while PrivateLink is being validated.
4) Run a latency + throughput test suite (we’ll provide containers you can run) to validate 95th/99th percentile latencies under burst and steady-state.

What we need from DataForge:
- Point of contact in NetOps to accept endpoint service and test security group entries.
- A window for POC traffic (non-prod) and a test VM for running our client harness (we can also run a synthetic harness from our side).
- Any compliance docs required for private link (we can provide SOC2 artifacts).

I’ll loop in our Solution Engineer and NetOps lead internally to map timeline. If agreeable, proposed next steps: 1) 30-min NetOps/SE call next week, 2) mutually-signed MOU for POC scope, 3) 2-week POC.

Attached: redwood-onramp-checklist.pdf (POC steps), topology-diagram.png (high-level sketch).

- Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

My quick asks:
- Kim: will we be able to publish the endpoint service from our account so external accounts can create interface endpoints? Any quota or cross-account limits to call out?
- Ben: commercial — if they want a Reserved bandwidth or SLA on PrivateLink endpoint, do we charge differently or add to Dedicated?
- Connor: Ops/infra — can we offer a managed VPN endpoint (terminated in our VPC) for them during POC and as a resilience path? What are the monitoring hooks?

Thanks — please reply with short bullets so I can consolidate before the DataForge NetOps call (target Mon 11/1).

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Onramp approach for private deployment (DataForge POC)

Stephanie — quick responses below.

Kimberly (answers):
- PrivateLink publish: yes, we can publish an interface endpoint service from our AWS account; cross-account creation is supported. We need the customer's VPC CIDR and the specific subnets they will use for the endpoint. Note: customer will need to accept the endpoint service in their account (simple API call/console).
- Quotas: interface endpoints per VPC default quota is 50 (soft limit), endpoint services per account are small; should be fine for a single-cust POC. If they want multiple AZ endpoints for HA, that's extra endpoint-hour cost but small.
- IP ownership and DNS: we recommend the customer either uses hosted zone private DNS or we provide a private hosted zone record so app code can resolve the endpoint name transparently.

Ben (commercial):
- PrivateLink billing: interface endpoints are charged by endpoint-hour + GB-in/GB-out. We can offer a POC credit; any production Reserved Bandwidth / SLA ask would map to a Dedicated contract (we should not promise new pricing without Sales approval).

Connor (ops):
- Managed VPN: yes, we can spin up a managed IPSec tunnel terminated in our VPC; will expose a public endpoint for them to peer to. We can provide monitoring via our Console (latency, packet drops) and alert on tunnel flaps. Ops will need to coordinate PSK or cert exchange and MTU tuning.

I’ll be on the NetOps call Monday.

- Kimberly

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@dataforge.io>, dataforge-infra@dataforge.io
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onramp approach for private deployment (quick ask) — next steps and action items

Oliver — thanks for the productive NetOps sync earlier. Agreed path and immediate actions below.

Agreed approach:
- Primary: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) into a Redwood-managed VPC exposing the model inference endpoint. This minimizes surface area and aligns with your compliance team.
- Secondary/fallback: Managed IPSec site-to-site VPN terminated in Redwood VPC for artifact pulls and as resilience in case of AZ-level issues.

Action items (owners / ETA):
1) Redwood: publish endpoint service + share ARN and docs (stephanie) — ETA: 2 business days.
2) DataForge NetOps: create interface endpoint and provide subnet IDs + security group rules (oliver) — ETA: 3 business days.
3) Redwood Ops: provision managed VPN endpoint, share PSK/cert exchange steps, and OpenVPN/strongSwan parameters (connor) — ETA: 4 business days.
4) Redwood SE: provide containerized latency/throughput harness and runbook (ben & stephanie) — ETA: 2 business days.
5) Legal/Commercial: draft short MOU for POC credit and data handling (ben) — ETA: 5 business days.

POC success criteria (mutually agreed):
- Latency: median < 35ms, p95 < 80ms from their app host to model endpoint for typical inference sizes.
- Throughput: sustained 150 req/s with 2s avg payloads without significant queueing.
- Security: endpoint reachable only from DataForge CIDRs; audit logs retained for 30 days.

I’ve attached the POC checklist and topology diagram for your NetOps team. If that all looks good we’ll start the ARN publish today and confirm the NetOps window.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

- Stephanie
